//: The public tier of knowledge: facts about tannergolden's setup that an agent cannot infer, installed into each app's home folder beside the rules. Facts, never rules; never personal context; never a private repository's name.
heading: Facts about this setup
intro: These are facts, not rules: they say how this setup works, so the rules above can be followed without guessing.
facts: Every tannergolden repository has one maintainer, so a pull request gets no second review: its checks are the only gate before the owner merges it.

Repositories built from the standards' templates integrate on `Development`, the default branch, through pull requests from `feat/*` and `bugfix/*` branches; `Experimental`, `Preview` and `Release` change only through pull requests too.
Release tags are created by workflows, never by hand.

The universal rules are rendered in tannergolden/intelligence and reach each repository as a pull request from `chore/intelligence`, so a hand edit inside an INTELLIGENCE block is undone by the next one.

In a Claude cloud session git's own identity is Claude's, so `git commit -s` and `git rebase --signoff` there would sign off as an AI; `--author` and `--trailer 'Signed-off-by: ...'` with your user's identity do not depend on it.
The home kit's guard hook denies force pushes, merges, `--no-verify`, AI sign-offs, destructive commands and edits inside INTELLIGENCE blocks, and each denial names the rule it enforces.
Repositories here carry `AGENTS.md` and no `CLAUDE.md`; Claude Code reads both only because the home kit sets its `instructionFiles` option.
Skills are written in tannergolden/intelligence under `skills/` and installed by the home kit; the `building-skills` skill says how to add one.
